Key Finding: Belonging to virtual communities increases affective commitment and drives peer-to-peer word-of-mouth recommendations among hobbyist consumers.
APA Reference: Royo-Vela, M., & Casamassima, P. (2011). The influence of belonging to virtual brand communities on consumers' affective commitment, satisfaction and word-of-mouth advertising. Online Information Review, 35(4), 517-542.

Key Finding: Consumers are more likely to follow peer advice in online communities when perceived trust and community identification are strong.
APA Reference: Casaló, L. V., Flavián, C., & Guinalíu, M. (2011). Understanding the intention to follow the advice obtained in an online travel community. Computers in Human Behavior, 27(2), 622-633. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chb.2010.04.013

Key Finding: Over one billion young people worldwide face potential hearing loss due to unsafe listening habits on personal audio devices and loud venues.
APA Reference: World Health Organization. (2021). World report on hearing. World Health Organization. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240020481

Key Finding: Local-first software architectures store primary data on client devices while synchronizing asynchronously to preserve offline usability and user ownership.
APA Reference: Kleppmann, M., Wiggins, A., van Hardenberg, P., & McGranaghan, M. (2019). Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud. Proceedings of the 2019 ACM SIGPLAN Onward!, 154-178. https://doi.org/10.1145/3359591.3359737

Key Finding: Listeners show a small statistically significant ability to discern high-resolution audio from standard quality, especially with listening experience.
APA Reference: Reiss, J. D. (2016). A meta-analysis of high resolution audio perceptual evaluation. Journal of the Audio Engineering Society, 64(6), 364-379. https://doi.org/10.17743/jaes.2016.0015

Key Finding: Hardware-software safe listening systems can track acoustic dosage across personal listening devices with less than one decibel of error.
APA Reference: Park, S., Lee, J., & Kim, H. (2023). Hearing care: Safe listening method and system for personal listening devices. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, 20(3), 2161. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20032161

Key Finding: For experience goods like personal audio equipment, moderate and detailed consumer reviews are perceived as significantly more helpful than extreme ratings.
APA Reference: Mudambi, S. M., & Schuff, D. (2010). What makes a helpful online review? A study of customer reviews on Amazon.com. MIS Quarterly, 34(1), 185-200. https://doi.org/10.25300/MISQ/2010/34.1.09

Key Finding: Online word-of-mouth reviews directly influence retail purchasing decisions, with critical reviews exerting a stronger weight than positive ones.
APA Reference: Chevalier, J. A., & Mayzlin, D. (2006). The effect of word of mouth on sales: Online book reviews. Journal of Marketing Research, 43(3), 345-354. https://doi.org/10.1509/jmkr.43.3.345

Key Finding: Unverified review platforms face higher rates of promotional self-boosting and competitor sabotage when commercial financial incentives exist.
APA Reference: Mayzlin, D., Dover, Y., & Chevalier, J. (2014). Promotional reviews: An empirical investigation of online review manipulation. American Economic Review, 104(8), 2421-2455. https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.104.8.2421

Key Finding: Global electronic waste reached 62 million tonnes in 2022, with small consumer electronics like earphones having very low formal recycling rates.
APA Reference: Baldé, C. P., Kuehr, R., Yamamoto, T., et al. (2024). The global e-waste monitor 2024. International Telecommunication Union and UNITAR. https://ewastemonitor.info/the-global-e-waste-monitor-2024/

Key Finding: Extending the lifespan of small consumer electronics through modular repairability and informed second-hand reuse reduces electronic waste generation.
APA Reference: Svensson-Höglund, S., Richter, J. L., Maitre-Ekern, E., Russell, J. D., Pihlajarinne, T., & Dalhammar, C. (2021). Barriers, enablers and market governance for repair of consumer electronics. Journal of Cleaner Production, 288, 125488.

Key Finding: Improper disposal of small electronic accessories releases hazardous heavy metals while wasting recoverable copper, gold, and rare-earth elements.
APA Reference: Forti, V., Baldé, C. P., Kuehr, R., & Bel, G. (2020). The global e-waste monitor 2020: Quantities, flows and the circular economy potential. United Nations University, ITU, and ISWA. https://ewastemonitor.info/gem-2020/

Key Finding: International technical standards jointly developed by WHO and ITU guide governments and manufacturers on safe personal audio system limits.
APA Reference: World Health Organization & International Telecommunication Union. (2019). Safe listening devices and systems: A WHO-ITU standard. World Health Organization. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241515276

Key Finding: National regulatory enforcement of data protection frameworks requires digital platforms to register processing systems and report security incidents.
APA Reference: National Privacy Commission. (2016). Implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 10173, known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012. Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines. https://privacy.gov.ph/

Key Finding: Cross-border digital platforms operating in Southeast Asia face evolving governance mandates regarding consumer protection and platform accountability.
APA Reference: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. (2019). Good practice guide on online consumer ratings and reviews. OECD Digital Economy Papers, No. 288. https://doi.org/10.1787/0f9362cf-en

Key Finding: Philippine law mandates explicit informed consent, data minimization, retention limits, and data portability rights for all personal data controllers.
APA Reference: Republic of the Philippines. (2012). Republic Act No. 10173: An Act protecting individual personal information in information and communications systems (Data Privacy Act of 2012). https://privacy.gov.ph/data-privacy-act/

Key Finding: The European Union General Data Protection Regulation enforces privacy by design, strict consent rules, and the right to erasure for online users.
APA Reference: European Parliament and Council of the European Union. (2016). Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data (GDPR). Official Journal of the European Union, L 119, 1-88.

Key Finding: Federal trade regulations strictly prohibit fabricated consumer reviews, undisclosed material connections, and deceptive review suppression on platforms.
APA Reference: Federal Trade Commission. (2023). Guides concerning the use of endorsements and testimonials in advertising, 16 C.F.R. Part 255. Federal Register, 88(142), 48092-48112. https://www.ftc.gov/

Key Finding: Releasing aggregated community datasets without enforcing k-anonymity thresholds enables re-identification of individuals through quasi-identifiers.
APA Reference: Sweeney, L. (2002). k-Anonymity: A model for protecting privacy. International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems, 10(5), 557-570. https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218488502001648

Key Finding: Online feedback mechanisms require careful institutional design to prevent strategic manipulation, retaliation, and unfair exclusion of newcomers.
APA Reference: Dellarocas, C. (2003). The digitization of word of mouth: Promise and challenges of online feedback mechanisms. Management Science, 49(10), 1407-1424. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.49.10.1407.17308

Key Finding: Content characteristics and reviewer transparency shape perceived usefulness and prevent deceptive framing in online consumer evaluations.
APA Reference: Willemsen, L. M., Neijens, P. C., Bronner, F., & de Ridder, J. A. (2011). Highly recommended! The content characteristics and perceived usefulness of online consumer reviews. Journal of Computer-Mediated Communication, 17(1), 19-38.
